345564.title: Central log-concavity conjecture for Gaussian binomial coefficients

actual_disposition.title: Central log-concavity conjecture for Gaussian binomial coefficients
actual_disposition.literal_statement:
For integers $n\geq 45$ and $13\leq k\leq n-13$, let

$$
\left[\begin{smallmatrix}n\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right]=\sum_r a_rq^r
$$

be the Gaussian binomial coefficient, so that $a_r=[q^r]\left[\begin{smallmatrix}n\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. The sequence of coefficients is **log-concave at $r$** when $a_r^2\geq a_{r-1}a_{r+1}$. **Central log-concavity conjecture.** For any fixed $n\geq 45$ and $13\leq k\leq n-13$, the coefficient sequence is log-concave at every integer $r$ satisfying

$$
25<r<k(n-k)-25.
$$

Computations up to $n=430$ support this conjecture. It concerns the failure of global log-concavity for Gaussian binomial coefficients and predicts log-concavity throughout a broad central range, but no proof or disproof is given here.
actual_disposition.reason: Uniform n>=45, 13<=k<=n-13 and every interior coefficient beyond distance25. Computation already through n430 is not proof; no uniform exact coefficient comparison established.

actual_disposition.title: Degree formulas for the Euclidean joint signature of a generic plane curve
actual_disposition.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{J}^{\mathcal{E}}_d$ denote the Euclidean joint signature for a generic plane curve of degree $d$. The multiprojective witness-set dimensions are $\boldsymbol{e}_1=(1,1,1,1,0,0)$ and $\boldsymbol{e}_2=(0,1,1,1,1,0)$. **Euclidean joint-signature degree conjecture.** For $d\ge 3$,

$$
\deg \overline{\mathcal{J}^{\mathcal{E}}_d}=12d(d^3-1),
$$

$$
\deg_{\boldsymbol{e}_1}\mathcal{J}^{\mathcal{E}}_d=8d^2(d^2-1),
$$

$$
\deg_{\boldsymbol{e}_2}\mathcal{J}^{\mathcal{E}}_d=4d(d-1)(3d^2+d-1).
$$

These formulas were suggested by monodromy computations, which were successfully run for curves of degree up to $10$; their validity for all $d\geq 3$ remains open.

335229.title: The outerplanar graph fractional-defect conjecture

actual_disposition.title: The outerplanar graph fractional-defect conjecture
actual_disposition.statement:
A $2$-coloring assigns each vertex a red usage in $[0,1]$, with blue usage $1-r(v)$; the defect of a vertex is the sum, over its neighbors, of the overlap in their color usages, and $D(G,2)$ is the minimum possible maximum defect over all such colorings of $G$. **Outerplanar graph fractional-defect conjecture.** For any outerplanar graph $G$,

$$
D(G,2)<2.
$$

Ordinary $2$-colorings of outerplanar graphs have defect at most $2$, and the fan examples show that the minimum defect can approach $2$ from below. The conjecture asks whether the bound is always strictly improvable.

336275.title: Butterfly trace conjecture

actual_disposition.title: Butterfly trace conjecture
actual_disposition.statement:
Let $B$ be the butterfly poset on four elements $a,b,c,d$, with $a,b<_B c,d$. For a family $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$, let $Tr_{n-1}(n,B)$ denote the maximum size of a family whose traces on all $(n-1)$-subsets contain no copy of $B$. **Butterfly trace conjecture.** If $n\geq 5$, then

$$
Tr_{n-1}(n,B)=\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}.
$$

The paper proves the related exact formula $Tr(n,B)=\lfloor 3n/2\rfloor+1$, but the asserted value for traces on $(n-1)$-subsets is posed as an open problem.

318669.title: General exact upper-bound conjecture for cliques on surfaces

actual_disposition.title: General exact upper-bound conjecture for cliques on surfaces
actual_disposition.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a surface with Euler characteristic $\chi$, let $\omega$ be the largest integer such that $K_\omega$ embeds in $\Sigma$, and let $G$ be a graph embeddable in $\Sigma$. Write $|V(G)|$ for the number of vertices of $G$.

**General exact upper-bound conjecture.** Every graph $G$ embeddable in $\Sigma$ has at most

$$
8|V(G)|-4(7+\sqrt{49-24\chi})+2^{(7+\sqrt{49-24\chi})/2}
$$

cliques, with equality if and only if $K_\omega$ triangulates $\Sigma$ and $G$ is obtained from $K_\omega$ by repeatedly splitting triangles.

The preceding bound $8(|V(G)|-\omega)+2^\omega$ is reported to fail for several surfaces without complete-graph triangulations, motivating this formulation in terms of the Euler characteristic. The conjecture gives the proposed exact extremal value for all surfaces.

actual_disposition.statement:
For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let a **non-flowerable collection** be a collection $\mathcal{C}$ of $n$ coins from which no flower, that is, no coin graph representation of a wheel graph, can be formed. Let $NF(\mathcal{C})$ be the maximum number of edges of a coin graph formed from coins in $\mathcal{C}$), and define

$$
NF(n)=\max\{NF(\mathcal{C}):\mathcal{C}\text{ is a non-flowerable collection of }n\text{ coins}\}.

$$

$$

actual_disposition.statement:
Let $G$ be a **Dirac graph**, meaning a graph on $n$ vertices with minimum degree at least $n/2$. 376428.title: The minimum-degree conjecture for colour-biased loose Hamilton cycles

actual_disposition.title: The minimum-degree conjecture for colour-biased loose Hamilton cycles
actual_disposition.statement:
Let $H$ be a red/blue coloured $3$-graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\delta_1(H)$ denote its minimum vertex degree. A **loose Hamilton cycle** is a cyclic ordering of the vertices in which every consecutive block of three vertices beginning at positions congruent to $1$ modulo $2$ forms an edge; it has $n/2$ edges. **The minimum-degree conjecture for colour-biased loose Hamilton cycles.** For every $\alpha>0$, there exist $\delta,n_0>0$ such that, whenever $n\geq n_0$ and

$$
\delta_1(H)\geq \left(\frac{7}{16}+\alpha\right)\binom{n}{2},
